items.exampleEn: Your toenails grow more slowly than your fingernails.
items.exampleZh: 腳趾甲長得比手指甲慢。

items.exampleEn: The village doctor in the novel could cure almost any malady.
items.exampleZh: 小說裡那位村醫幾乎什麼病都治得好。

items.exampleEn: This ointment smells strongly of mint.
items.exampleZh: 這種藥膏有濃濃的薄荷味。

items.exampleEn: Today, factories can make penicillin in very large amounts.
items.exampleZh: 如今工廠可以大量生產盤尼西林。

items.exampleEn: Fifty years ago, this disease was incurable, but now there is a cure.
items.exampleZh: 五十年前這種病無法治癒，但現在已經有治療方法了。
items.glossZh: 無法治癒的；無可救藥的

items.exampleEn: The machine measures the respiration rate of the plants in the lab.
items.exampleZh: 那台儀器測量實驗室裡植物的呼吸速率。

items.exampleEn: Corporal punishment means hitting someone as a punishment.
items.exampleZh: 體罰是指以打人作為懲罰。

items.exampleEn: Bulimia was first described as a separate illness in 1979.
items.exampleZh: 暴食症在 1979 年首次被描述為一種獨立的疾病。

items.sentenceEn: Penicillin was one of the first medicines to fight germs.
items.sentenceZh: 盤尼西林是最早用來對抗細菌的藥物之一。

items.audioEn: The pharmacy on the corner sells this ointment, but it closes at eight.
items.audioZh: 轉角的藥局有賣這種藥膏，不過八點就關門了。

items.sentenceEn: Corporal punishment is not allowed in schools in many countries.
items.sentenceZh: 許多國家的學校都不允許體罰。

items.sentenceEn: My sister is an incurable romantic who cries at every love story.
items.sentenceZh: 我的姊妹是個無可救藥的浪漫派，看每部愛情故事都會哭。

items.stemEn: Scientists use the word ____ for the process in which our cells use oxygen to turn food into energy.
items.stemZh: 科學家用「呼吸作用」這個詞，指細胞利用氧氣把食物轉化成能量的過程。

items.stemEn: He cut his ____ short before putting on his new running shoes.
items.stemZh: 他穿上新跑鞋前，先把腳趾甲剪短。

items.passageEn: Our health class this term, held in a cozy room on the top floor, looked at the history of medicine. We learned how penicillin was discovered when a scientist noticed that something growing on a dish was killing germs. We also read about old remedies: people once rubbed strange ointments on their skin for every small malady. Our teacher explained respiration and how the lungs bring oxygen into the bloodstream. In another lesson, a guest speaker talked about eating disorders such as bulimia and how researchers study them. We also discussed how many countries have banned corporal punishment in schools. Even my best friend, whose love of jokes is incurable, listened carefully. My only small complaint is the long reading list.
items.passageZh: 這學期的健康課在頂樓一間溫馨的教室上，探討醫學的歷史。我們學到盤尼西林是怎麼被發現的：一位科學家注意到培養皿上長出的東西殺死了細菌。我們也讀到古老的療法：以前的人一有小病小痛，就在皮膚上塗抹奇怪的藥膏。老師講解了呼吸作用，以及肺如何把氧氣送進血液。另一堂課，一位客座講者談到暴食症等飲食疾患，以及研究人員如何研究它們。我們也討論了許多國家已經禁止學校體罰。就連我那個愛開玩笑到無可救藥的好朋友都聽得很專心。我唯一的小抱怨是書單太長。

questions.questionZh: 盤尼西林是怎麼被發現的？
options: 有人在菜園的泥土裡找到的
醫生在研究古老的藥膏時
學生在學校的實驗室裡做實驗時
培養皿上長出的東西殺死細菌

questions.questionZh: 作者的好朋友是什麼樣的人？
options: 非常害羞，在課堂上很少說話
常常遲到又不寫回家作業
